related_questions.snippet: Manage Symptoms Most people with COVID-19 have mild illness and can recover at home. You can treat symptoms with over-the-counter medicines, such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen, to help feel better.

related_questions.question: How long are you contagious with COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People with COVID-19 can be infectious from 1–2 days before and up to 8–10 days after symptoms begin. The majority of transmission appears to occur during the early periods of infection, particularly in the 1–2 days before symptoms start and within the first few days of symptom onset.

related_questions.question: How to recover quickly from COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: To recover quickly from COVID-19, focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management. Getting plenty of sleep, staying hydrated, and taking over-the-counter medications for fever or body aches can help accelerate recovery. If you're vaccinated, you may experience less severe symptoms and recover faster according to WebMD.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Prioritize sleep and avoid strenuous activities. Aim for more than the recommended 7-9 hours of sleep for adults.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, especially if you have a fever.

list.title: Symptom Relief:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage fever and body aches.

list.title: Hygiene:
list.snippet: Practice good hygiene by washing your hands frequently and avoiding close contact with others.

list.title: Monitor Your Health:
list.snippet: Pay attention to your symptoms and seek medical advice if they worsen or if you experience any emergency symptoms.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to get over COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The duration of COVID-19 recovery varies, but most people with mild cases recover within one to two weeks. However, some individuals may experience symptoms for longer, with research suggesting that 30-50% of people could have symptoms lasting longer than 12 weeks (3 months), according to Nova Scotia Health Library.
Factors like age, overall health, and the severity of the initial infection influence recovery time. Common symptoms like fatigue, headache, and troubled breathing are more likely to linger.

The CDC recommends isolating until you've been fever-free for 24 hours (without medication), symptoms are improving, and it's been at least five days since symptoms started. Even after ending isolation, it's advised to avoid close contact with vulnerable individuals and to wear a mask indoors for at least 11 days.
